correctness.rationale: Two-sided Brownian stochastic integral conditioned on the marked Poisson history yields a finite-all-moment stationary solution. Strict contraction gives synchronous L2 coupling and uniqueness. The modulus reflected-diffusion generator involves only absolute multiplier marks. Conditional stationary Gaussian variance involves only mark squares. The conditional nth-moment leading coefficient is the exact compound-Poisson product expectation exp(-r(1-E[Q^n])t). Its rates converge to r by uniform contraction, and compact moment determinacy plus a Vandermonde argument establish infinite/finite inverse uniqueness. Generator identities yield exact signed/squared covariance rates and three-observable deterministic-factor inversion. 211 exact checker assertions reproduce the algebra; stochastic and infinite claims are proved analytically.

originality.rationale: Existing positive-factor partial-reset papers and the related fixed signed-factor stationary Fourier product determine stationary laws and basic moments; generic polynomial-process papers cover correlation calculations. The inspected literature and accessible own claim history do not cover the conjunction of signed-random-factor complete modulus-path indistinguishability and the full-law/finite-atomic/two-correlation inverse theorem. The fixed-sign stationary marginal equivalence is explicitly treated as background and not as the original contribution. Priority risk remains for broader inverse-problem literature.

value.rationale: A physical partial-reset particle can undergo backtracking either with or without a sign reversal. Entire stationary magnitude trajectories and stationary signed histograms cannot resolve that distinction, giving a sharp experimental identifiability obstruction. Exact sign-sensitive conditional moment rates overcome the obstruction; unknown r and D are jointly recovered, at most m multiplier atoms require only 2m-1 rates when r is known, and a deterministic factor requires just two covariance decays and one variance. This is a motivated distinguishability classification rather than a small numeric gain or stationary-density recomputation; finite-sample performance is not claimed.
